## The corrected-PE face gravity work (`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT`) {#sec-ch06-dwork}

### Summary

With `gravity-work: face`, snapy books the work gravity does on the flow in the form of a flux
difference of potential energy across each cell's $x_1$ faces (the face form). This scheme adds
one term to that work in every cell, @eq-ch06-dwork-d, where $\dot\rho$ is the stage's $x_1$ density tendency,
$s_i$ the centroid slope of @eq-ch06-dwork-slope and $\sigma_i^2$[^rg-24c85d83151c] the variance of $x_1$ over the cell. The added
term is the work done by moving the mass of a cell whose density is not uniform inside it.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Adds one term to the face form, @eq-ch06-dwork-d, so the booked work is fourth order in every cell.

**Data.** Reads the stage's $x_1$ density tendency and the $x_1$ grid; writes $g_1\sigma^2s[\dot\rho]\Delta t$ into the energy row.

**Placement.** Each stage, in the gravity-work block of `HydroImpl::forward`; with an implicit scheme partly in the VIC.

**Activation.** `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` (on by default) with `gravity-work: face`, $g_1\ne0$, a grid with an $x_1$ measure.

**Guarantee / limits.** $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ to the bound below per stage and step; work $O(h^4)$; $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ not conserved.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch06-dwork-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\Delta_{+,0}=x_{1,1}-x_{1,0}$ and $\Delta_{+,1}=x_{1,2}-x_{1,1}$ [m] the
first two centroid spacings at a column end (appendix A's $\Delta_+$ at cells 0 and 1, used only in the end-cell
slope); $r_{\mathrm c}$ [m] the volume centroid and $x_{1v}$ [m] the stored cell centre `x1v` on a `gnomonic-equiangle`
block; $o_i=r_{\mathrm c,i}-x_{1v,i}$ [m] the offset of the volume centroid from the stored centre, which is
appendix A's $\delta_i$[^rg-8b7387f6bab7] where `x1v` is the face midpoint and zero where it is the centroid; $b_i$ the per-cell term of
the conservation sum and $N_{\mathrm{rd}}$ its number of roundings. Every other symbol of this
section is appendix A’s ($P$, $\mathcal P$[^rg-84698c2c1f47], $\mathrm{PE}_d$[^rg-d054fdb5ce7a], $\sigma_i^2$, $s_i$, $\mathcal N_i$[^rg-972d04f188e1], $\Delta_\pm$[^rg-233d4794e1ca], $\mathsf S$[^rg-477c78c44075],
$\tilde{\mathsf S}$, $W^{\mathrm D}$, $\delta_i$, $\Delta t_c$[^rg-f6811c76094b], $\boldsymbol\delta_i$[^rg-db3e7925d5ab], $\vartheta$[^rg-bd680c20cc4f], $\lambda_w$[^rg-e41403c7e700]).

The face form conserves total energy $E$ plus the discrete potential energy $\mathrm{PE}_d$ exactly, but
$\mathrm{PE}_d$ is itself only a second-order approximation of the true potential energy of the cell averages.
The face form therefore books a gravity work with an $O(h^2)$ error in every cell: the trapezoid term
$\tfrac{h^2}{12}\partial_1^2F$, plus two $O(h^2/r)$ curvature terms on spherical-polar grids. The cp3/cp5/weno5
reconstructions remove part of it with the curvature flux $\mathcal K$ (the face form), but that flux is zero at
walls, which leaves the two wall cells of every column first order. This scheme replaces $\mathrm{PE}_d$ by a
fourth-order potential energy $P$ and books exactly the work that conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$. The result is a gravity work
that is $O(h^4)$ relative to the exact work of the scheme's own $x_1$ mass fluxes, in every cell, measured on
uniform Cartesian and spherical-polar grids; and $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ conserved to round-off on a closed column, in every RK[^rg-d61c45b5aed8]
stage, explicit and implicit. It does not make the energy equation fourth order: the fluxes $F_{i\pm1/2}$ keep
the reconstruction's and the Riemann solver's error.

`gravity-work: face` is the default (`gravity_work`, {{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}; struct default
`gravity_work`, {{< code src/forcing/forcing.hpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::gravity_work >}}), so a run that does not state the key, on a Cartesian, spherical-polar or
`gnomonic-equiangle` (cubed-sphere) grid, uses this scheme unless it is switched off; a run that states
`gravity-work: cell` is unaffected. On the cubed sphere `x1v` is the face midpoint, not the volume centroid, and the
work gains the centroid-offset term of @eq-ch06-dwork-cs. Only on a grid with no $x_1$ measure for the scheme
(cylindrical) does setup warn once and keep the plain face work. With it
active the curvature flux $\mathcal K$ is turned off, because the scheme already removes the term $\mathcal K$
removes and the two together are back to $O(h^2)$; it never meets the gravity-work fixer, which
runs only with `gravity-work: cell`; and with an implicit scheme part of it is booked inside the vertical
implicit operator (the VIC gravity work). Under it the conserved invariant is $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$, the cycle diagnostics log $P$ as
`pe=`, and every $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ check measures the wrong quantity.

*Aliases.* "Leg D" of the gravity-work round, hence "scheme D" in commit messages; "option F" in
`docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` §7, whose "option D" is
a different, rejected two-point weight; "corrected-PE work", and "radial-exact" in identifiers.[^ch06-dwork-credit]

[^ch06-dwork-credit]: The scheme came with the gravity-work round of chengcli/snapy; chengcli/snapy#303 (closing
    chengcli/snapy#300) carried it to the cubed sphere, made `face` the default form and gave the seam cells of a
    split column the centred slope.

### Derivation

Every closed form in this layer is checked by `d_face_work_pe_check.py`; the claim tags `[Cn]` point at its
output lines; every `[Cn]` number has the same provenance.[^ch06-dwork-chk]

[^ch06-dwork-chk]: [sha: snapy@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5, ported line for line; at internal $x_1$ seams
    the port takes the one-sided
    slope, which the code keeps only on a periodic column (see the Check below); deck: the check itself; run:
    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch06/checks/d_face_work_pe_check.py`, CPU, double, 1 process; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6,
    sympy 1.14.0; output identical to the committed file]. Output `d_face_work_pe_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C11]`.
Fitted orders use the last three resolutions ($n_1$ = 64, 128, 256) unless stated. Units: $g_1$ [m s$^{-2}$],
$\rho$[^rg-c9f0740df1f4] [kg m$^{-3}$], $F$ [kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$], $h$ and $x_1$ [m], $\sigma^2$ [m$^2$], $\phi$ [m$^2$ s$^{-2}$],
$W$ [W m$^{-3}$]; $E$ is the total energy density [J m$^{-3}$], and $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ and
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ are the integrated sums of the chapter preamble, with $E_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_iV_iE_i$ [J, per
unit horizontal area on Cartesian grids and per steradian on spherical-polar]. The
executable check is nondimensional, with $g_1=-10$ and scale height $H=1$.

The continuous budget, the exact work of one cell @eq-ch06-dwork-template and the booked work
@eq-ch06-dwork-booked are derived in the chapter preamble: whatever discrete potential energy $P$ a form uses, the
work @eq-ch06-dwork-booked conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ exactly and is as accurate as $P$ is. The design problem of this section
is to choose a $P_i$ that is accurate and computable from cell averages.

#### The face form is $P = \mathrm{PE}_d$

The discrete continuity equation in $x_1$ is

$$
V_i\dot\rho_i = -\Delta_i[AF],
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-continuity}

with $F_{i\pm1/2}$ the total mass flux density the Riemann solver returns: the dry row plus every mass-carrying
species row $n = 1..N_y$, after the positivity limiter and sedimentation. That sum is `vertical_mass_flux1`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}), the $F$ every form in this section is handed.
Take $P_i = V_i\bar\rho_i\phi_i$ with
$\phi_i=\phi(x_{1,i})$ at the volume centroid. Then $\dot P_i = V_i\dot\rho_i\phi_i = -\phi_i\Delta_i[AF]$ and
@eq-ch06-dwork-booked gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
W^{\mathrm{face}}_i &= \frac{1}{V_i}\Big[\phi_i\,\Delta_i[AF] - \Delta_i[A\phi F]\Big] \\
&= \frac{g_1}{V_i}\Big[(x_{1,i+1/2}-x_{1,i})A_{i+1/2}F_{i+1/2} + (x_{1,i}-x_{1,i-1/2})A_{i-1/2}F_{i-1/2}\Big],
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-face}

the second form from $\phi_i - \phi_{i\pm1/2} = g_1(x_{1,i\pm1/2}-x_{1,i})$. @eq-ch06-dwork-face is computed as
`face_gravity_work` in
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}
(times $\Delta t$). The face form conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ exactly, by @eq-ch06-dwork-booked.

$\mathrm{PE}_d$ is the exact $\int\rho\phi\,\mathrm{d}V$ of a piecewise-constant density, so it misses the in-cell
density gradient. On a uniform Cartesian grid @eq-ch06-dwork-face is the trapezoid rule,
$W^{\mathrm{face}}_i = g_1(F_{i+1/2}+F_{i-1/2})/2$, with error $g_1\tfrac{h^2}{12}\partial_1^2F$ in every cell. On
a spherical-polar grid two more terms appear
(`docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` §2, eq. 2):

$$
\frac{W^{\mathrm{face}}_i - g_1\langle F\rangle_{V_i}}{g_1}
= \frac{h^2}{12}\partial_1^2F + \frac{h^2}{6r^{\mathrm{m}}}\partial_1F - \frac{h^2}{6(r^{\mathrm{m}})^2}F + O(h^4).
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-faceerr}

`[C6]` measures the face form at second order in interior and wall cells on both grids.

#### The potential energy of a cell to fourth order

Let $\rho(x_1)$ be smooth inside cell $i$ and expand it about the centroid $x_{1,i}$[^rg-41e20e055363], with the derivatives taken
at $x_{1,i}$:
$\rho = \rho(x_{1,i}) + \partial_1\rho\,(x_1-x_{1,i}) + \tfrac12\partial_1^2\rho\,(x_1-x_{1,i})^2
+ \tfrac16\partial_1^3\rho\,(x_1-x_{1,i})^3 + \dots$. With $\phi = -g_1x_1$,

$$
\mathcal P_i = -g_1\int_{V_i}\rho\,x_1\,\mathrm{d}V
= -g_1\Big[x_{1,i}\int_{V_i}\rho\,\mathrm{d}V + \int_{V_i}\rho\,(x_1-x_{1,i})\,\mathrm{d}V\Big].
$$

The first integral is $V_i\bar\rho_i$ exactly, with $\bar\rho_i$ the cell average, so the first term is
$V_i\bar\rho_i\phi_i$. In the second, the centroid makes the first moment vanish,
$\int_{V_i}(x_1-x_{1,i})\,\mathrm{d}V=0$. Of the remaining moments the second is $V_i\sigma_i^2$ with
$\sigma_i^2 = \langle(x_1-x_{1,i})^2\rangle_{V_i}$; the third is zero on a Cartesian grid and $O(h^4/r)\,V_i$ on
spherical-polar; the fourth is $O(h^4)V_i$. Hence

$$
\mathcal P_i = V_i\Big[\bar\rho_i\phi_i - g_1\sigma_i^2\,\partial_1\rho(x_{1,i})\Big] + O(h^4V_i).
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-pe4}

On a uniform Cartesian cell the remainder is exactly $-g_1\tfrac{h^5}{480}\partial_1^3\rho + O(h^7)$. On a
spherical-polar cell the $h^0$ to $h^3$ terms of the remainder per unit volume vanish identically `[C3]`.
$\mathrm{PE}_d$ keeps only the first term, which is why it is $O(h^2)$.

The cell variance $\sigma_i^2$ is $h_i^2/12$ on Cartesian grids. On spherical-polar grids, per steradian, with
$r^{\mathrm{m}}$ the cell midpoint and $h$ the width, it is

$$
\begin{aligned}
V &= (r^{\mathrm{m}})^2h + \tfrac{h^3}{12}, \\
\delta_i &= x_{1,i}-r^{\mathrm{m}} = \frac{r^{\mathrm{m}}h^3}{6V}, \\
\sigma^2 &= \frac{(r^{\mathrm{m}})^2h^3/12 + h^5/80}{V} - \delta_i^2 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-variance}

@eq-ch06-dwork-variance is computed as `x1_variance` in
{{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp x1_variance >}}.
It is the exact variance on the $r^2$ measure about the volume centroid (`x1v` on a spherical-polar grid is that
centroid). It is written about the midpoint so that nothing cancels at
$r/h\gg1$: the relative error is $1.7\times10^{-16}$ at $r/h=10^6$ `[C1]`.

$\partial_1\rho(x_{1,i})$ is not known; only cell averages are. Replace it by the centroid slope

$$
s_i[\bar\rho] = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x_1}\Big|_{x_{1,i}}\ \text{of the quadratic through }
(x_{1,l},\bar\rho_l),\ l\in\mathcal N_i,
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-slope}

@eq-ch06-dwork-slope is computed as `centroid_slope` in
{{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp centroid_slope >}}.
The stencil depends on the cell's place in the array it is given: $\mathcal N_i = \{i-1,i,i+1\}$ inside it, and
$\mathcal N_0 = \{0,1,2\}$, $\mathcal N_{n_1-1} = \{n_1-3,n_1-2,n_1-1\}$, one-sided, at its two $x_1$ ends. A
block's own ends are those of the array only at a physical wall: at an internal $x_1$ seam the caller passes the
neighbour's cell as well, so the seam cell takes the centred stencil (`corrected_pe_work_seam`, below).
With $\Delta_- = x_{1,i}-x_{1,i-1}$ and $\Delta_+ = x_{1,i+1}-x_{1,i}$ the interior weights are

$$
s_i[\bar\rho] = -\frac{\Delta_+}{\Delta_-(\Delta_-+\Delta_+)}\bar\rho_{i-1}
+ \frac{\Delta_+-\Delta_-}{\Delta_-\Delta_+}\bar\rho_i
+ \frac{\Delta_-}{\Delta_+(\Delta_-+\Delta_+)}\bar\rho_{i+1},
$$

and at the first cell, with $\Delta_{+,0} = x_{1,1}-x_{1,0}$ and $\Delta_{+,1} = x_{1,2}-x_{1,1}$,

$$
s_0[\bar\rho] = -\frac{2\Delta_{+,0}+\Delta_{+,1}}{\Delta_{+,0}(\Delta_{+,0}+\Delta_{+,1})}\bar\rho_0
+ \frac{\Delta_{+,0}+\Delta_{+,1}}{\Delta_{+,0}\Delta_{+,1}}\bar\rho_1
- \frac{\Delta_{+,0}}{(\Delta_{+,0}+\Delta_{+,1})\Delta_{+,1}}\bar\rho_2,
$$

mirrored at the last cell. `[C2]` checks these weights against the derivative of the Lagrange quadratic.

Each stencil annihilates a constant and is exact for a quadratic. A cell average differs from the point value at
the centroid by $\tfrac12\partial_1^2\rho\,\sigma^2+\dots$, a smooth $O(h^2)$ amount when $h$ varies smoothly, so
$s_i[\bar\rho] = \partial_1\rho(x_{1,i}) + O(h^2)$ in interior and end cells alike. `[C4]` measures orders 1.77
to 1.99 for this error, on a stretched Cartesian grid and a spherical column; the spherical fit is still
pre-asymptotic at $n_1$ = 64 to 256. Then $\sigma_i^2s_i = \sigma_i^2\,\partial_1\rho + O(h^4)$, and the
corrected discrete potential energy

$$
P[\bar\rho] = \sum_iV_i\Big[\bar\rho_i\phi_i - g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\bar\rho]\Big] = \mathcal P + O(h^4)
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-pe}

is fourth-order accurate. `[C4]` measures $|P-\mathcal P|/|\mathcal P|$ at orders 4.08 (stretched Cartesian) and
4.62 (spherical, inner radius $5H$), against 2.00 for $\mathrm{PE}_d$.

$P$ is linear in $\bar\rho$ and reads no cell outside the block: no ghost cells. That is the wall closure. From
here on this section uses only cell averages, so the bar is dropped: $\rho_i$ is the cell average.

#### The work that conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$

Insert $P_i = V_i[\rho_i\phi_i - g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\rho]]$ into @eq-ch06-dwork-booked. Because $s_i$ is linear,
$\dot P_i = V_i[\dot\rho_i\phi_i - g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\dot\rho]]$, and comparing with @eq-ch06-dwork-face,

$$
\begin{aligned}
W^{\mathrm{D}}_i &= W^{\mathrm{face}}_i + g_1\,\sigma_i^2\,s_i[\dot\rho], \\
V_i\dot\rho_i &= -\Delta_i[AF].
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-d}

@eq-ch06-dwork-d is computed by `corrected_pe_work` in
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}},
which adds `corrected_pe_work` (`corrected_pe_work_seam` at an $x_1$ seam) of `drho = -dt * vertical_mass_div`, i.e. $\Delta t\,g_1\sigma^2s[\dot\rho]$, to the
face work. This is the whole scheme. It changes only the energy row: mass and momentum are untouched. At rest
($F\equiv0$, so $\dot\rho=0$) it adds exactly zero.

#### The cubed sphere: the centroid-offset term

On a `gnomonic-equiangle` block $x_1$ is the radius, and `face_area1` and `cell_volume` carry the same solid angle
per column, so per steradian $A$, $V$ and $\sigma^2$ are those of a spherical-polar column. The one difference is
where `x1v` sits: it is the face midpoint $r^{\mathrm{m}}$, not the volume centroid $r_c$
(`docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` §12.1). The expansion of @eq-ch06-dwork-pe4 is about
$r_c$ and does not depend on `x1v`, and because $\phi$ is linear, $\phi(r_c) = \phi(x_{1v}) - g_1o$
exactly. Hence, with the code offset $o_i$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
o_i &= r_{c,i} - x_{1v,i} = \frac{r^{\mathrm{m}}h^3}{6V} + (r^{\mathrm{m}} - x_{1v,i})
= \frac{h^2}{6r^{\mathrm{m}}} + O(h^4/r^3), \\
P[\rho] &= \sum_iV_i\Big[\rho_i\phi(x_{1v,i}) - g_1o_i\rho_i - g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\rho]\Big], \\
W^{\mathrm{D}}_i &= W^{\mathrm{face}}_i + g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\dot\rho] + g_1o_i\dot\rho_i .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-cs}

Here $\sigma_i^2$ is still the variance about $r_c$ (@eq-ch06-dwork-variance), $W^{\mathrm{face}}$ uses
$\phi(x_{1v})$ as the code does, and $s_i$ stays on the `x1v` nodes: $o$ varies by $O(h^3/r^2)$ across a
three-cell stencil, so $\sigma^2s$ moves by $O(h^4/r^2)$, below the $O(h^4)$ of $P$ (same note, §12.3). On Cartesian
and spherical-polar grids `x1v` is the centroid, $o\equiv0$, and @eq-ch06-dwork-cs is @eq-ch06-dwork-pe and @eq-ch06-dwork-d.
@eq-ch06-dwork-cs is computed as `x1_centroid_offset` in {{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp x1_centroid_offset >}}, written about the midpoint so that it does
not cancel at large $r$[^rg-96220307ca24], and the term $g_1o_i\dot\rho_i\Delta t$ is added by `corrected_pe_work` in
{{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp corrected_pe_work >}} for the `radial_mid` measure only, so on Cartesian and spherical-polar grids the work is the slope term alone. The measure is chosen by `x1_measure` in {{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp x1_measure >}}, one shared
helper for every site that books or logs the work.

The change of $P$ equals the booked work term by term, as in @eq-ch06-dwork-booked. $P$ is linear in $\rho$, so over
a stage $\Delta P_i = V_i[\Delta\rho_i\phi(x_{1v,i}) - g_1o_i\Delta\rho_i - g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\Delta\rho]]$.
The face form books $-V_i\Delta\rho_i\phi(x_{1v,i}) - \Delta t\,\Delta_i[A\phi F]$, the slope term
$+g_1V_i\sigma_i^2s_i[\Delta\rho]$, the centroid term $+g_1V_io_i\Delta\rho_i$. Each cancels its own part of
$\Delta P_i$, which leaves $-\Delta t\,\Delta_i[A\phi F]$, and that telescopes to the walls (same note, §12.5a).
The new term is diagonal: it uses only the cell's own density change. It enters with the same sign and weights
the four places that book or log the work: the explicit face work, the diagonal of the VIC energy row, the
post-solve remainder and the logged `pe=`. With the term in the work but not in $P$, or the reverse, each cell
keeps $\pm g_1V_io_i\Delta\rho_i$, an $O(h^2/r)$ defect. Left out of both, $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ still closes, but the work
error is $-g_1o\dot\rho$, second order with a $1/r$ coefficient (same note, §12.7).

`d_cs_centroid_term_check.py` ports the four helpers and checks both statements.[^ch06-dwork-cs-chk]

[^ch06-dwork-cs-chk]: [sha: the formulas of snapy@ccf40f9565642c32be69f4b9ef0cfa6daff3f201, where the slope is evaluated
    through a cached stencil with
    the same weights and the same order of operations; deck: the check itself; run:
    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch06/checks/d_cs_centroid_term_check.py`, CPU, double, 1 process; Python 3.14.7, numpy 2.5.1;
    output identical to the committed file]. Output `d_cs_centroid_term_check.out`, lines `[CS1]`–`[CS2]`.

`[CS1]`: one stage with random interior fluxes and closed walls gives
$(\Delta E_{\mathrm{grav}}+\Delta P)/\sum|WV\Delta t|$ = $8.8\times10^{-16}$, $-1.9\times10^{-14}$ and
$1.5\times10^{-13}$ at $r/H$ = 5, 60 and 1000, the last two at the cancellation floor of the large $\phi$; with the
term in the work but not in $P$, $-1.3\times10^{-5}$, $-1.7\times10^{-7}$ and $-4.4\times10^{-10}$. `[CS2]`:
$|P-\mathcal P|/|\mathcal P|$ for $\rho = e^{-(r-R)/H}$ at $R = 5H$, $n_1$ = 16 to 128, falls at orders 3.47, 3.77,
3.89 with the term in $P$ and 2.01, 2.01, 2.00 without it. The derivation note's own replica,
`docs/derivations/cubed_sphere_centroid_term.py@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f`, checks the same identities with sympy.

#### Conservation, exactly

Sum @eq-ch06-dwork-d times $V_i$ over a closed column. By construction @eq-ch06-dwork-booked,
$\sum_iW^{\mathrm{D}}_iV_i + \dot P = -\sum_i\Delta_i[A\phi F]
= -(A\phi F)_{\mathrm{top}} + (A\phi F)_{\mathrm{bottom}} = 0$. No property of the slope weights, the grid or the
flux enters. The energy fluxes other than gravity telescope as well. So in exact arithmetic
$\sum_iV_iE_i + P$ is constant over one evaluation of the right-hand side.

In floating point the same telescoping argument gives a derived bound. Each cell's term
$b_i=V_i\big(\Delta t\,W^{\mathrm D}_i+\Delta P_i/V_i\big)+(\text{other energy fluxes})$ is computed with at most $N_{\mathrm{rd}}$
roundings, the column adds $n_1$ of them, and the stage combination rounds each $E_i$ five times (`wght0`, [`pyharp integrator.cpp:120`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L120)), as in
@sec-ch06-face:

$$
\big\lvert\widehat{\Delta(E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P)}\big\rvert\le(N_{\mathrm{rd}}+n_1)\,\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_i\lvert b_i\rvert
+5\cdot\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_iV_i\lvert E_i\rvert\quad\text{per stage}.
$$

The slope term adds a three-point stencil per cell to $N_{\mathrm{rd}}$; $N_{\mathrm{rd}}$ is not counted here. `[C7]` reports
$\lvert\Delta(E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P)\rvert/\lvert E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P\rvert$ per step. In that normalisation the energy-update term
alone gives $15\cdot\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_iV_i\lvert E_i\rvert/\lvert E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P\rvert$ over the three rk3 stages,
$1.7\times10^{-15}$ when $E$ dominates the sum; `[C7]` measures at most $3.5\times10^{-16}$ per step on a stretched
Cartesian column, inside it.

snapy's RK stage is $\mathbf U \leftarrow w_0^{(s)}\mathbf U^n + w_1^{(s)}\mathbf U
+ w_2^{(s)}\Delta t\,\mathcal L(\mathbf U)$ with $w_0^{(s)}+w_1^{(s)}=1$. For rk3 the weights
$(w_0^{(s)},w_1^{(s)},w_2^{(s)})$ are $(0,1,1)$, $(\tfrac34,\tfrac14,\tfrac14)$ and
$(\tfrac13,\tfrac23,\tfrac23)$, set in `IntegratorImpl` at
[`pyharp integrator.cpp:33-61`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L33-L61).
Write $\mathcal E(\mathbf U) = \sum_iV_iE_i + P[\rho]$. $\mathcal E$[^rg-add6046816b3] is linear in $\mathbf U$, and
$\mathcal E(\Delta t\,\mathcal L) = 0$ by the identity above. Then
$\mathcal E(\mathbf U^{\mathrm{new}}) = w_0^{(s)}\mathcal E(\mathbf U^n) + w_1^{(s)}\mathcal E(\mathbf U)$, which
equals $\mathcal E(\mathbf U^n)$ whenever $\mathcal E(\mathbf U)=\mathcal E(\mathbf U^n)$. By induction over the
stages, $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ is constant over the step to round-off.

`[C7]` steps closed columns 20 times with arbitrary nonlinear fluxes. The max per-step
$|\Delta^{\mathrm{stg}}(E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P)|/|E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P|$ is $\le3.5\times10^{-16}$ on every case: Cartesian stretched; spherical with
inner radius over scale height 1, 5 and 1000; two $x_1$ blocks; a 2-D box. Over the same steps
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ drifts by $10^{-8}$ to $10^{-5}$ per step.

$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ is not conserved by this scheme. Since
$\mathrm{PE}_d = P + g_1\sum_iV_i\sigma_i^2s_i[\rho]$, it changes per stage by

$$
\Delta^{\mathrm{stg}}(E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d) = +g_1\sum_iV_i\sigma_i^2s_i[\Delta^{\mathrm{stg}}\rho],
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-ped-change}

the $O(h^2)$ error of $\mathrm{PE}_d$ itself. `[C7]` checks @eq-ch06-dwork-ped-change on one stage of every case,
to $\le5.3\times10^{-17}$ of the summed magnitudes of its terms. This is the intended behaviour, not a defect:
$\mathrm{PE}_d$ is the wrong target. At
`docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` §7 and §8.6 this change
carries the same plus sign; check the note's current head before publication.

#### Accuracy

From @eq-ch06-dwork-booked, $W^{\mathrm{D}}_iV_i - g_1V_i\langle F\rangle_{V_i}
= \tfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\mathcal P_i - P_i)$. By @eq-ch06-dwork-pe4 and @eq-ch06-dwork-pe,
$\mathcal P_i - P_i = -g_1V_i\sigma_i^2(\partial_1\rho(x_{1,i}) - s_i[\rho]) + O(h^4V_i)$, which is linear in
$\rho$. Its time derivative is the same expression applied to the density tendency. For a smooth flux field
$F(x_1)$ the discrete tendency @eq-ch06-dwork-continuity is the exact cell average of
$-A^{-1}\partial_1(AF)$, so that expression is $O(h^4V_i)$ too:

$$
W^{\mathrm{D}}_i = g_1\langle F\rangle_{V_i} + O(h^4) \quad \text{in every cell, wall cells included,}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-order}

where $F$ is the flux field the scheme is handed. To leading order,
$\sigma^2s[\dot\rho] = -\tfrac{h^2}{12}(\partial_1^2F + 2\partial_1F/r - 2F/r^2)$, which is minus
@eq-ch06-dwork-faceerr: the scheme cancels all three $O(h^2)$ terms of the face form, the trapezoid term and both
curvature terms.

`[C6]` uses the profile $F = e^{-z/H}\sin(\pi z/4H)$ on $[0,4H]$, which vanishes at both walls, on uniform grids.
It compares the booked work with the exact cell averages; values are given at $n_1$ = 16 and 256.

| form and grid | interior | order | wall cells | order |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| face, spherical, inner radius $5H$ | 4.44e-3 $\to$ 2.50e-5 | 1.95 | 5.81e-3 $\to$ 2.54e-5 | 1.98 |
| this scheme, spherical, inner radius $5H$ | 3.47e-5 $\to$ 5.35e-10 | 4.00 | 5.37e-5 $\to$ 1.79e-10 | 4.49 |
| face, Cartesian | 4.99e-3 $\to$ 3.11e-5 | 1.94 | 7.02e-3 $\to$ 3.17e-5 | 1.98 |
| this scheme, Cartesian | 7.44e-5 $\to$ 1.16e-9 | 4.00 | 1.29e-4 $\to$ 1.91e-9 | 4.02 |

: Max-norm error $\lVert W-g_1\langle F\rangle_V\rVert_\infty/|g_1|$ of the booked work against the exact cell
average, at $n_1$ = 16 and 256, from check line `[C6]`. {#tbl-ch06-dwork-order}

#### Uniform-grid closed forms

On a uniform Cartesian column, @eq-ch06-dwork-d can be written in face fluxes. Use
$\dot\rho_l = -(F_{l+1/2}-F_{l-1/2})/h$, $\sigma^2 = h^2/12$, the interior slope
$s_i = (\dot\rho_{i+1}-\dot\rho_{i-1})/2h$, and the wall slope
$s_0 = (-3\dot\rho_0+4\dot\rho_1-\dot\rho_2)/2h$ with $F_{-1/2}=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{W^{\mathrm{D}}_i}{g_1} &= \frac{F_{i+1/2}+F_{i-1/2}}{2}
- \frac{F_{i+3/2}-F_{i+1/2}-F_{i-1/2}+F_{i-3/2}}{24}, \\
\frac{W^{\mathrm{D}}_0}{g_1} &= \frac{19F_{1/2}-5F_{3/2}+F_{5/2}}{24},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-uniform}

and $W^{\mathrm{D}}_{n_1-1}$ is the mirror image of $W^{\mathrm{D}}_0$. Cells 1 and $n_1-2$ use the interior form
with the wall flux, which is zero. `[C5]` checks both forms symbolically and their accuracy: the wall form is
exact for $F = z, z^2, z^3$ with $F(0)=0$, and its error for $z^4$ is $\tfrac{19}{30}h^4$; the interior form has
no error terms below $h^4$.

Take a face-flux wave $F = \cos(2\pi x_1/\lambda_w)$ and put cell $i$ at $x_1=0$, with
$\vartheta = \pi h/\lambda_w$. Then the added term over the face term in @eq-ch06-dwork-uniform is

$$
\frac{1-\cos3\vartheta/\cos\vartheta}{12} = \frac{\sin^2\vartheta}{3}.
$$

This is $\vartheta^2/3$ for long waves, so $O(h^2)$, but $\tfrac14$ at wavelength $3h$ and up to $\tfrac13$ as
the wavelength approaches $2h$ `[C9]`. The added term is a small correction only for resolved flow. At the grid
scale it is a fixed fraction of the face work, which matters for the implicit solver.

#### Horizontal directions and several blocks

In 2-D and 3-D, the $x_2$ and $x_3$ fluxes move mass between columns at the same $x_1$ level $i$ and book no
gravity work. On spherical-polar grids $V_{ijk} = \varpi_{jk}\,V^{(1)}_i$; on Cartesian grids the same holds with
$\varpi_{jk}=\Delta x_2\Delta x_3$. And $h_i$[^rg-0708b6d1b931], $\sigma_i^2$ and the stencil @eq-ch06-dwork-slope are the same in
every column. Because $s$ is linear,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{j,k}P_{jk} &= \sum_iV^{(1)}_i\Big[\phi_i\bar M_i - g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\bar M]\Big], \\
\bar M_i &= \sum_{j,k}\varpi_{jk}\rho_{ijk}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$\bar M_i$ is the level's total mass, which horizontal fluxes conserve (periodic or closed lateral boundaries).
So $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ stays exact. `[C7]` checks this on a 2-D box with periodic $x_2$ fluxes: $3.4\times10^{-16}$ per step.

For blocks split in $x_1$ (explicit runs only; an implicit scheme refuses any $x_1$ split), a seam cell takes the
centred slope that a single block takes: the explicit work exchanges one row of the stage's density change with the
$x_1$ neighbour (a ghost $\dot\rho$ cannot be computed locally: it needs the mass flux on the ghost cell's far face,
which no block computes), and the logged `pe=` reads the ghost density, which the mesh exchanges after every
stage. Both call `corrected_pe_work_seam` in {{< code src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp corrected_pe_work_seam >}}. The slope stays one-sided only at physical walls, so
$P$ and the work are those of one block on any $x_1$ decomposition, and global $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ is exact. A periodic $x_1$
column keeps one-sided slopes at its block edges (Limits layer); there $P$ is a sum of per-block functionals.
`[C10]` measures what that choice costs, the functional difference $|P_{\mathrm{split}}-P_{\mathrm{one}}|/|P|$
with one-sided seam slopes, falling from $2.6\times10^{-8}$ at $n_1$ = 32 to $5.3\times10^{-13}$ at 256, order 5.2
(fit over all four resolutions); `[C7]`, two blocks with one-sided seams, $2.2\times10^{-16}$, shows that $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ is
exact with either seam slope.

#### How the scheme enters the vertical implicit solve

With `implicit-scheme` $\neq 0$, the vertical implicit correction (VIC, the vertical implicit solve) solves each column for a new
stage increment $\boldsymbol\delta_i$. The explicit increment $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$[^rg-83a8e2b01f50] is its right-hand side, and
under rk3 and rk3s4 the solve is handed $\Delta t_c = w_2^{(s)}\Delta t$, set as `dt_corr` in
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
Row $i$ of the block-tridiagonal system reads

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf A_i\boldsymbol\delta_i + \mathsf B_i\boldsymbol\delta_{i-1} + \mathsf C_i\boldsymbol\delta_{i+1}
&= \Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}_i/\Delta t_c, \\
\mathsf A_i &= \mathsf I/\Delta t_c + \text{Jacobian terms}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-vicrow}

@eq-ch06-dwork-vicrow is assembled from the right-hand side `rhs` in
{{< code src/implicit/forward_sweep_impl.h ForwardSweep >}},
with the block convention of `delta` in
{{< code src/implicit/forward_sweep_impl.h ForwardSweep >}}.
Its unknowns are, in order, the total mass, the normal momentum, the two tangential momenta (full VIC only) and
the energy. The solved energy is written back from `delta` as the stage's energy increment in
{{< code src/implicit/vic_redistribute_impl.h vic_redistribute_cell >}}.
With `gravity-work: face` the energy row already contains the face form for the mass the solve moves
(derived in @sec-ch06-vic), assembled under
the `face_work` flag in
{{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}
for full VIC and
{{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_partial_impl.h vic_assemble_partial_impl >}}
for partial VIC.

Booking the scheme only after the solve would treat $g_1\sigma^2s[\Delta\rho_{\mathrm{solve}}]$ explicitly, and
by @eq-ch06-dwork-uniform that term is a quarter to a third of the face work for a grid-scale density change, not
an $O(h^2)$ correction. The face work it accompanies is implicit, and stable at vertical acoustic Courant numbers
of hundreds. A discretely balanced $11.3H$ rest column (implicit-scheme 9) with the term booked only after the
solve grew from round-off to $\max|v_1| = 1.3\times10^{-7}$ m s$^{-1}$: at step 13 at Courant 197 and step 9 at
Courant 250, in both geometries, against $\le4.9\times10^{-9}$ m s$^{-1}$ with the switch off. Dropping only the
post-solve term restored the switch-off level; dropping only the explicit term did not.[^ch06-dwork-tall]

[^ch06-dwork-tall]: sha: the parent of snapy@f256ab51fa400641360d16ea3611e78eba85ccc5, run sha not recorded; deck:
    `tests/test_implicit_gravity_tall_column.py`; run: CPU; source: `docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` §10. A
    re-run needs `f256ab51fa400641360d16ea3611e78eba85ccc5^` or a mutation of the pinned code that drops the operator
    coupling.

The matrix is built by `couple_radial_exact` in
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}.
Let $\mathsf S$ be the slope matrix, $(\mathsf S q)_i = s_i[q] = \sum_l\mathsf S_{il}q_l$; the code builds its
transpose as `centroid_slope(eye(n1), x1v)`. Inside a block row $i$ of $\mathsf S$ has three entries on the
tridiagonal. At the two end cells the one-sided slope reads a third cell, which a block-tridiagonal system cannot
hold. The matrix therefore holds a lumped $\tilde{\mathsf S}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tilde{\mathsf S}_{il} &= \mathsf S_{il}\ (|i-l|\le1), \\
\tilde{\mathsf S}_{01} &= \mathsf S_{01}+\mathsf S_{02}, \\
\tilde{\mathsf S}_{n_1-1,n_1-2} &= \mathsf S_{n_1-1,n_1-2}+\mathsf S_{n_1-1,n_1-3}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-lumped}

The third weight is moved onto the neighbour, in the `rx_lo`, `rx_hi` lumping block of
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}.
Each cell's weights still sum to zero, so $\tilde s$ still annihilates a constant `[C8]`. At the end cells
$\tilde s$ is not a consistent slope, though:
$\tilde s_0 = \tfrac{2\Delta_{+,0}+\Delta_{+,1}}{\Delta_{+,0}(\Delta_{+,0}+\Delta_{+,1})}(\rho_1-\rho_0)$, which is $\tfrac{3}{2h}(\rho_1-\rho_0)$ on a uniform grid
`[C8]`. The post-solve remainder below is therefore not small in the two end cells. That part of the scheme stays
explicit at the grid scale; the tall-column test is the evidence that this is stable.

The energy row gains a coupling to the total-mass unknown, and its right side gains the matching term in
`rx_mass0`, at
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf A_i^{(E,\rho)} &\leftarrow \mathsf A_i^{(E,\rho)} - \frac{g_1\sigma_i^2\tilde{\mathsf S}_{ii}}{\Delta t_c}, \\
\mathsf B_i^{(E,\rho)} &\leftarrow \mathsf B_i^{(E,\rho)} - \frac{g_1\sigma_i^2\tilde{\mathsf S}_{i,i-1}}{\Delta t_c}, \\
\mathsf C_i^{(E,\rho)} &\leftarrow \mathsf C_i^{(E,\rho)} - \frac{g_1\sigma_i^2\tilde{\mathsf S}_{i,i+1}}{\Delta t_c}, \\
\frac{\Delta E^{(0)}_i}{\Delta t_c} &\leftarrow \frac{\Delta E^{(0)}_i}{\Delta t_c}
- \frac{g_1\sigma_i^2\tilde s_i[\Delta\rho^{(0)}]}{\Delta t_c},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-couple}

with $\Delta\rho^{(0)}$ the total-mass part of $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$. On the cubed sphere the diagonal weight `rx_mid` also
gains $g_1o_i$ of @eq-ch06-dwork-cs, in `couple_radial_exact` at
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}. That term is diagonal, so the matrix holds it exactly, without lumping:
wherever @eq-ch06-dwork-couple to @eq-ch06-dwork-remainder write $g_1\sigma_i^2\tilde s_i[\cdot]$, read
$g_1(\sigma_i^2\tilde s_i+\delta_i)[\cdot]$ there, and the post-solve `corrected_pe_work` call at
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}} carries the same $g_1o_i$ on the solved change. Only fluid cells get these terms
(`rx_fluid`). Reading the energy row of @eq-ch06-dwork-vicrow with @eq-ch06-dwork-couple:

$$
\delta E_i = \Delta E^{(0)}_i + g_1\sigma_i^2\,\tilde s_i\big[\delta\rho - \Delta\rho^{(0)}\big]
- \Delta t_c\,(\text{Jacobian terms}\cdot\boldsymbol\delta)_{E,i}.
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-energyrow}

The energy row of @eq-ch06-dwork-energyrow is the row the entry updates of `couple_radial_exact`
({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}) leave behind, in fluid cells only.
The solve books the work of the mass it moves, $\delta\rho-\Delta\rho^{(0)}$, implicitly. `[C11]` assembles a toy
column with exactly these entry updates and right-hand side, solves it in the convention of
@eq-ch06-dwork-vicrow, and recovers @eq-ch06-dwork-energyrow to $9\times10^{-15}$. Flipping the coupling's sign
or swapping its lower and upper weights leaves an $O(1)$ residual.

After the solve the raw solution is redistributed among the constituents and clamped where a constituent would go
negative (the vertical implicit solve). Let $\Delta\rho_i$[^rg-5fbd06ccd73e] be the solved density change, `du` summed over the mass rows after
redistribution. The code's `moved` is `du - du0`, i.e. $\Delta\rho_i-\Delta\rho^{(0)}$, and it can differ from
$\delta\rho-\Delta\rho^{(0)}$. After the redistribution the code adds, in fluid cells, the remainder

$$
g_1\sigma_i^2\Big(s_i[\Delta\rho_i-\Delta\rho^{(0)}] - \tilde s_i[\delta\rho-\Delta\rho^{(0)}]\Big),
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-remainder}

computed from `moved` in
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}},
so the implicit part books exactly $g_1\sigma^2s[\Delta\rho_i-\Delta\rho^{(0)}]$ in fluid cells, the work of the
mass actually moved. With the explicit part, the stage total is @eq-ch06-dwork-d for the full $x_1$ density
change, and $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ closes. Lumping only changes how much of the work the solve sees implicitly, never the total.

`[C8]` makes two checks on this. First, a mock solve whose redistribution changes the face masses (a binding
clamp at one face, a shifted mass at another): its $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ defect is round-off ($2.4\times10^{-16}$ and
$5.5\times10^{-14}$ against $\sum|\Delta E\,V|$ of 0.35 and 18). Second, the same solve booked on the raw change
instead of the solved one leaves defects of $4.4\times10^{-7}$ and $2.6\times10^{-4}$. The sum of the matrix part
and @eq-ch06-dwork-remainder is an identity by construction and is only printed.

In an immersed solid cell the solid rows of the matrix are set by `setIdentity` over $\Delta t_c$ in
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cpp vic_assemble_partial_cpu >}}
and
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cpp vic_assemble_full_cpu >}}.
The coupling and its right-side term are masked there (`rx_fluid`), and the post-solve remainder is gated to zero
in the same remainder block, because the slope stencil of a solid cell would read fluid neighbours. A fluid cell
next to a solid keeps its centred stencil, which then reads the solid's density change, which is zero.

**What is exact and what is truncated.** Exact to round-off, on any grid, per stage and per step, explicit and
implicit: the conservation of $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ on closed columns and on several $x_1$ blocks, and the identity
@eq-ch06-dwork-ped-change. Truncated: $P$ approximates the true potential energy to $O(h^4)$
(@eq-ch06-dwork-pe); the booked work approximates the exact work of the scheme's own mass fluxes to $O(h^4)$ in
every cell (@eq-ch06-dwork-order), for smooth fields on smoothly varying grids. A column split in $x_1$ equals
the unsplit one, because the seam cell takes the centred slope; only at the block edges of a periodic $x_1$ column,
which keep the one-sided slope, does the split differ, at $O(h^4)$. This derivation is independently corroborated for the Cartesian case by a different
construction in `sources/gw__NEXTPR_indep_cartesian_gravity_work_weight.md` §§2.3-2.6; its §4.4 disputes several
claims of the derivation note and must be dispositioned before this section is approved.

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
The identities above are checked by `d_face_work_pe_check.py`, 11 claims, all passing (count:
`python3 d_face_work_pe_check.py | grep -c '^\[C[0-9]*\] PASS'`). It ports the formulas of the code at the pin
on Cartesian and spherical-polar grids. At internal $x_1$ seams it takes the one-sided slope, which the code keeps
only at the block edges of a periodic column; its claim C10 and the two-block case of its claim C7 therefore
describe that case, not the centred seam slope. The cubed-sphere centroid term is checked by
`d_cs_centroid_term_check.py`, 2 claims.
:::

### Numerical method

@fig-ch06-dwork-stencil shows what the scheme reads: an interior cell, a wall cell, an $x_1$ block seam and the
implicit matrix row. @fig-ch06-dwork-order shows the order of the work it books.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch06-dwork-stencil
#| fig-cap: "The stencil of the corrected-PE face work, on four panels. (a) An interior cell: the face form reads the two face fluxes (orange triangles), and the added term reads the densities of cells i-1, i, i+1 (bluish-green circles), hence four faces. (b) The bottom wall cell: the slope is one-sided on cells 0, 1, 2, the wall face carries no flux, and no ghost cell (hatched, light reddish purple) is read. (c) One-sided slopes at the block edges, the case of a periodic x1 column: each block takes one-sided slopes at its own ends, so P splits into a sum over blocks. At any other internal seam the seam cell exchanges one row of the stage's density change with its neighbour and takes the centred slope (not drawn), so P is that of one block; in both cases the seam face's potential flux cancels between the blocks. (d) The VIC energy row's coupling to the total-mass unknown: row i holds the weights of the cells in the slope of cell i, the one-sided end weight (hatched) is lumped onto the neighbour (arrow), and the post-solve term books the difference."
#| fig-alt: "Four panels. Three cartoons of cells and faces with cell values as circles and face values as triangles, ghost cells hatched, the wall a thick black line and the block seam a dashed line; then a matrix-row diagram with an arrow showing the lumped end weight."
```

Nondimensional, with $g_1=-10$ and $H=1$; the data of @fig-ch06-dwork-order are the committed output of the
executable check at the formulas of the pin, the same check line `[C6]` as
@tbl-ch06-dwork-order.

In the code the interior cells of a block in $x_1$ are `is` $\le$ index < `ie`, with `is = il()` and
`ie = iu() + 1`. Math cell $i = 0..n_1-1$ is code index `is + i`; face $i-\tfrac12$ is code face index `is + i`.

| quantity | lives at | from |
|---|---|---|
| $F_{i\pm1/2}$ | $x_1$ faces, owned faces of the block | Riemann solver, then the positivity limiter and sedimentation; summed over the dry row and the species rows `ICY`..`ICY+`$N_y$`-1` |
| $A_{i\pm1/2}$[^rg-bb05fe6a8840], $V_i$ | faces, cells | `face_area1()`, `cell_volume()` |
| $\phi_{i\pm1/2}$, $\phi_i$ | faces, cell centroids | $-g_1$`x1f`, $-g_1$`x1v` |
| $\dot\rho_i\,\Delta t$ | interior cells | `-dt * vertical_mass_div` |
| $\sigma_i^2$ | interior cells | `x1_variance` on the block's interior faces |
| $s_i[\cdot]$ | interior cells | `centroid_slope` on the block's interior centroids |
| $W^{\mathrm{D}}_i\,\Delta t$ | interior cells, energy row | added to `du[IPR]` |

: Where each quantity of the scheme lives. {#tbl-ch06-dwork-lives}

**Walls.** The only data the scheme reads are interior densities, in the form of tendencies, and the grid
geometry. At a closed wall the slope is one-sided, conservation uses only $F=0$ on the wall face, and the wall
cells are $O(h^4)$ (`[C6]`: orders 4.49 spherical and 4.02 Cartesian). That is what makes it a wall closure for
the gravity work. The cp3/cp5/weno5 curvature flux $\mathcal K$ needs a value at the wall face and is set to
zero there, which leaves its wall cells first order: Cartesian first cell $1.65\times10^{-2}$ $\to$
$2.05\times10^{-3}$, order 1.00, $n_1$ 16 $\to$ 128
(`docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` §8.3, §8.7).[^ch06-dwork-replica] The scheme does not use $\mathcal K$: the `curv_flux1` branch in
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}
turns it off when the scheme is active.

[^ch06-dwork-replica]: deck: `docs/derivations/optionF_replica.py@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f`, printed label §6; base sha
    8cea3ae5a8297c82205c1cb9da03681f2343c0dc, which is not the code pin; run not recorded, so this is re-run work
    before approval.

On open (non-reflecting) $x_1$ boundaries the same one-sided stencil is used, but there the boundary face's
$A\phi F$ does not vanish. $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ then changes by exactly the potential-energy flux through the boundary, which
is the physical budget. Not separately tested; see the Limits layer.

**Block seams in $x_1$.** At an internal $x_1$ seam the explicit work fills a full-length array with the stage's
density change, exchanges one row with each $x_1$ neighbour (`_x1_ghost_rows`) and calls `corrected_pe_work_seam`,
so a seam cell takes the centred slope, in {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}; at a physical wall the slope stays one-sided. The
seams are found by `x1_neighbors` in {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::x1_neighbors >}}, which returns $\{-1,-1\}$ on a periodic $x_1$ column, so
the internal seams of a periodic column keep the one-sided slope; setup then warns once, in the `TORCH_WARN_ONCE`
at {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}, because $-g_1x_1$ jumps at the periodic face and $P$ is not defined. The logged `pe=` uses the
same helper on the ghost densities, so the booked work and the logged $P$ agree and are those of one block on any
decomposition. An implicit scheme refuses a block whose $x_1$ faces are not both physical boundaries, in the
`TORCH_CHECK` at {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}, so the VIC row and its post-solve term never meet a seam. A gnomonic-equiangle
layout holds one block in $x_1$, so there the one-sided slope sits only at the two walls
(`docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` §12.6).

**When it runs in a stage.** Within `HydroImpl::forward` the scheme runs in step (6), external forcing, after the
$x_1$, $x_2$, $x_3$ fluxes and the tracer positivity limiter, after the flux divergence, and after every forcing
module, including the const-gravity cell work $\rho v_1g_1\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}$, with $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}$ the non-hydrostatic
factor (key `non-hydrostatic`), in `ConstGravityImpl::forward` at
{{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityImpl::forward >}}.
The energy correction booked is $W^{\mathrm{D}}_i\Delta t - W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i\Delta t$: the cell work is
removed and the face form plus this scheme is put in its place, as `gravity_energy_correction` in
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
With a non-hydrostatic factor $\alpha_{\mathrm{nh}}<1$ the removed cell work includes the hydrostatic-split part of
`original_gravity_work`, computed at
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}};
that part is not added by a forcing module, so the `rho_grav` block at
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}
adds it right after the correction is computed. In an explicit run, or `face` with `implicit-scheme` 0, the
correction is added to `du[IPR]` after the implicit step if any, at
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
With `face` and `implicit-scheme` $\neq0$, selected by `face_work_in_operator()`, it is added to `du` *before*
the solve, at
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}};
the solve then sees, and inverts, the face-form energy including the explicit term, and adds its own implicit
term.

| order of $W^{\mathrm{D}}-g_1\langle F\rangle$ | where | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | interior, Cartesian and spherical-polar, uniform | `[C6]` 4.00, 4.00 |
| 4 | wall cells, uniform | `[C6]` 4.49 spherical, 4.02 Cartesian |
| none: split equals one block | $x_1$ block seam, state, split vs one block | `test_x1_seam_split` (`radial_exact_split_gap`) asserts a gap of exactly 0 at $n_1$ 32, 64, 128; with one-sided seam slopes (periodic columns only) the functional gap `[C10]` falls at order 5.2 |
| 4 | wall and interior cells, cubed sphere, explicit | Evidence: wall 4.03, interior 3.87 to 4.00 |
| about 2 | wall cells, cubed sphere, VIC | Evidence: 1.4 to 2.0; cause in the Limits layer |
| 4 for $P$ | non-uniform $x_1$ grid, smooth stretching | `[C4]` $P$: 4.08 on a stretched grid; the work on non-uniform grids is not measured |
| not established | non-smooth $x_1$ grid, jumps in $h$ | see the Limits layer |

: Order of accuracy of the booked work, by region and grid. {#tbl-ch06-dwork-orders}

### Code

**A minimal input.** The corrected-PE work needs no YAML[^rg-20d0ad55a777] of its own: it acts with `gravity-work: face` (the
default) on Cartesian, spherical-polar and gnomonic-equiangle grids, and is switched by the environment.

```yaml
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8        # gravity-work: face by default
# environment: SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT unset or 1 (on), 0/false/off/no (off)
```

The plain face form of @sec-ch06-face runs with the switch off, from `build/bin` of a build at the pin
([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)): `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0 ./straka.release straka_single.yaml`.

**What the code refuses or warns, and why.** `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` is read once per process, because every
block must book the same work ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::gravity_work_radial_exact >}}). Nothing is
refused. `HydroImpl::reset` warns once in two cases ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}):

1. With a periodic $x_1$: $-g_1x_1$ jumps there, so the corrected $P$ is not defined.
2. On a grid with no $x_1$ measure: the plain face work is kept.

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch06-dwork-d** ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}), the
single-block branch (a split column calls `corrected_pe_work_seam` instead):

```cpp
bool radial_exact = !gw_cell && radial_exact_work();
if (radial_exact) {
  auto drho = -dt * vertical_mass_div;
  auto measure = x1_measure(pmb->pcoord->options->type());
  auto [below, above] = x1_neighbors();
  if (below < 0 && above < 0) {
    face_gravity_work +=
        corrected_pe_work(drho, pmb->pcoord->x1f, pmb->pcoord->x1v, is, ie,
                          grav1, measure, &_pe_work);
  } else {
    ...   // an x1 seam: the neighbour's row one cell past it, then corrected_pe_work_seam
  }
}
```

The code comments are left out and the seam branch is elided. `drho` is $\Delta t\,\dot\rho_i=-\Delta t\,\Delta_i[AF]/V_i$,
and the call adds $\Delta t\,g_1\sigma^2s[\dot\rho]$, plus $g_1\delta\,\dot\rho$ on `radial_mid`.

pyharp@4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29. The symbol column is the citation's anchor: it is the identifier
the cited symbol contains.

: Code map of the corrected-PE face gravity work. {#tbl-ch06-dwork-code}

**Walk-through in step order.**

1. In the `HydroImpl` constructor, `gravity-work` is validated, `gravity_work_fixer` is forced off for face
   forms at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}},
   a grid with no form for the scheme warns once in the `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}},
   and an implicit scheme with a split $x_1$ is refused by the `TORCH_CHECK` at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}.
2. Each stage, `HydroImpl::forward` computes the total $x_1$ mass flux after the positivity limiter and
   sedimentation, as `vertical_mass_flux1` at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
3. It forms $\Delta t\,W^{\mathrm{face}}$ as `face_gravity_work` at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
4. If `radial_exact_work()`, it adds `corrected_pe_work` (`corrected_pe_work_seam` at an $x_1$ seam) of `drho = -dt * vertical_mass_div` at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}
   and skips the `curv_flux1` term at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
5. It replaces the cell work by the face form, as `gravity_energy_correction` at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
6. It adds `gravity_energy_correction` to the energy before the implicit solve at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}
   or, from the same `gravity_energy_correction`, after it at
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
7. In the VIC, `couple_radial_exact` adds the matrix coupling and right side after the assembly at
   {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}},
   and the remainder, the `corrected_pe_work` of the `moved` mass, after the redistribution at
   {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}.
8. The cycle diagnostics log $P$ under `radial_exact_work` at
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}},
   so the logged `ie=` + `pe=` is the conserved $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$.

### Tests

Tolerances are relative to $|E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P|$ unless stated. Python tests run each switch arm in a child process, because
the switch is read once per process. C++ ctest names end in the lower-case build type (`release` in CI[^rg-9642e02413d9]).

  $3.5\times10^{-14}$ (scale 2119) [same note §10; deck: that test; run: sha not recorded $\to$ **re-run**].
- **Missing evidence.** The onset-rate numbers of §11.2 of the derivation note and the coarse polytrope
  kinetic-energy numbers carry no deck or run. The onset numbers are $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff}}n_1^2$ at $n_1$
  = 16, 32, 64: $+0.0306, +0.0158, +0.0080$ without the scheme and $-0.00092, -0.00020, -0.00004$ with it. They
  are re-run from a committed deck or removed before approval; check the note's current head before publication.

**Coverage.** CPU: all of the above. CUDA: `test_gravity_work_radial_exact_cuda_python` and the `_cuda` arms of
`test_x1_seam_split`, registered only with `-DCUDA=ON` and skipped without a device. Several ranks:
`test_x1_seam_split_mp_radial_exact`, 2 ranks under torchrun. One entry runs this scheme with
`SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=1`: `test_pref_local_seam_flux_covariance` (registered in
{{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}), whose Cartesian deck states no `gravity-work` key
and sets `grav1` to $-9.81$ ({{< code tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp kDriftYaml >}}), so the scheme is
on by default. It asserts that four $x_1$ blocks match one block after 200 steps to $10^{-12}$; it does not check
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$. No test runs this scheme with `SNAP_WB_REF4` or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` on: their seam arms pass
`cell` to `split_gap` ({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp centroid_exact_split_matches_one_block >}} and, for `SNAP_WB_REF4`,
`split_gap` {{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp wb_ref4_flag_at_the_seam_split_matches_one_block >}}); see the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The limits a user can hit by configuration: a periodic $x_1$ column keeps one-sided seam slopes (and warns), a grid
with no $x_1$ measure (cylindrical) keeps the plain face work, `face-wallc` does not get this scheme, a block with fewer than three $x_1$ cells books nothing beyond the face form, and under this scheme
every $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ check — including `gravity_work_defect()` — measures the wrong invariant.
:::

1. **Seams and periodic $x_1$.** A column split in $x_1$ gives the one-block state
   (explicit runs; an implicit scheme refuses any $x_1$ split). With a periodic $x_1$ boundary the internal seams
   keep the one-sided slope, so the split differs from one block there; a gravitating periodic $x_1$ column has no
   single-valued potential ($-g_1x_1$ jumps at the periodic face), so $P$ is not defined in any case, and setup
   warns once. Documented, by design.
2. **Cubed sphere.** The scheme runs on `gnomonic-equiangle` grids with the centroid-offset term of
   @eq-ch06-dwork-cs. A lone gnomonic block with reflecting lateral walls loses mass under lateral flow, with the
   switch on or off,[^ch06-dwork-301] so its $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ cannot close; the single-block test
   uses radial flow only, and lateral flow and panel seams are covered by the six-panel test. Grids with no $x_1$
   measure (cylindrical) keep the plain face work and warn.
3. **`face-wallc`** does not get this scheme: it keeps the cell work in the wall cells by design.
4. **Short blocks.** For $n_1<3$ cells in a block the slope is zero and nothing is booked beyond the face form.
5. **Non-smooth $x_1$ grids.** The $O(h^2)$ accuracy of $s$ assumes that the cell-average offset
   $\tfrac12\partial_1^2\rho\,\sigma^2$ varies smoothly, i.e. that $h$ varies smoothly. Across a jump in $h$ the
   slope error is $O(h)$ and $P$ drops to $O(h^3)$ locally. Conservation is unaffected. Not measured; nor is the
   work on smoothly stretched grids.
6. **Order of the energy equation.** The scheme makes the gravity work fourth-order consistent with the mass
   fluxes. The fluxes themselves keep the order of the reconstruction and the Riemann solver (@sec-ch04).
7. **The end cells of the implicit solve.** The lumped slope $\tilde s$ is not a consistent slope in the two end
   cells, so part of the scheme stays explicit there at the grid scale. The tall-column test passes; no stability
   bound is derived. The VIC wall cells converge at order about 2, not 4 (measured 1.4 to 2.0 on the cubed sphere,
   Evidence): the implicit correction flux is first-order upwind and $O(\Delta t)$, so its grid-scale part is
   $O(\Delta t\,h)$ and the wall work is second order at fixed CFL[^rg-21882d810815]; with $\Delta t\sim h^2$ the order rises toward
   3. Cartesian grids show the same.[^ch06-dwork-302]
8. **Open $x_1$ boundaries.** $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ changes by the boundary potential-energy flux, as it should. No test covers
   the scheme with an outflow $x_1$ boundary.
9. **Diagnostics and oracles.** Under this scheme `gravity_work_defect()` and any $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ check measure
   the wrong invariant. Tests that check the plain face form set the switch to 0 explicitly.
10. **Explicit solids.** The explicit path books the scheme in every interior cell, solid or not; immersed solid
    cells are refilled every step. The VIC gates them. The explicit path with solids is not separately tested.
11. **Remaining error of the onset rate.** With the wall closure and this scheme, the linear onset rate of
    convection keeps a second-order truncation error that the face and cell forms share. The convergence table in
    `docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f` §11.3 is filled from runs at commits
    that are not the code pin, so its numbers are **re-run** work before approval; check the note's current head
    before publication.
12. **Untested switch combinations.** This scheme with `SNAP_WB_REF4`, `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` or
    `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE`, and on moist columns with several mass rows, is covered by no ctest entry; with
    `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` only the split-column check `test_pref_local_seam_flux_covariance` covers it (Evidence),
    and no entry checks $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ there. The onset numbers above used `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` and `SNAP_WB_REF4`; the note
    names their deck, but no ctest covers the combination. See the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
13. **Float32.** $\sigma^2$ is written without cancellation (@eq-ch06-dwork-variance), but the $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$ identity has
    been checked only in double precision.
14. **Open disagreement in the sources.** `sources/gw__NEXTPR_indep_cartesian_gravity_work_weight.md` §4.4 lists
    claims it holds to be wrong or under-qualified in the derivation note this section rests on, in particular
    §4.4(a) on the Cartesian "conflict" sentence. Each item is dispositioned before this section is approved.

[^ch06-dwork-301]: Recorded in chengcli/snapy#301.

[^ch06-dwork-302]: Recorded in chengcli/snapy#302; the cause and the Cartesian result are from the Limits of the body
    of chengcli/snapy#303.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-24c85d83151c]: $\sigma_i^2$ — variance of $x_1$ about the centroid over cell $i$ on its own measure, $\langle (x_1-x_{1,i})^2\rangle_{V_i}$

[^rg-8b7387f6bab7]: $\delta_i$ — centroid offset $x_{1,i}-x^{\mathrm{m}}_{1,i}$ (zero on Cartesian); [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp#L95-L105)

[^rg-84698c2c1f47]: $\mathcal P$ — the exact potential energy $\int\rho\phi\,dV$ of a smooth density field; notation only; see @sec-appa

[^rg-d054fdb5ce7a]: $\mathrm{PE}_d$ — discrete potential energy $\sum_iV_i\rho_i\phi_i$

[^rg-972d04f188e1]: $\mathcal N_i$ — the stencil set of the centroid slope of cell $i$ (stencil cells indexed by $l$); [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp#L60-L87)

[^rg-233d4794e1ca]: $\Delta_\pm$ — centroid spacings $x_{1,i+1}-x_{1,i}$ ($+$) and $x_{1,i}-x_{1,i-1}$ ($-$), used in non-uniform stencils; never $h_\pm$, which would read as cell widths; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/src/hydro/gravity_work_radial.hpp#L66-L71)

[^rg-477c78c44075]: $\mathsf S$ — the matrix of $s$: $(\mathsf S q)_i = s_i[q] = \sum_l\mathsf S_{il}q_l$ (row $i$: the weights of the cells $l$ in the slope of $i$; the code stores the transpose); $\tilde{\mathsf S}$ likewise for $\tilde s$; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp#L349-L374)

[^rg-f6811c76094b]: $\Delta t_c$ — the time step handed to the implicit solve: $w_{2,s}\Delta t$ under rk3 and rk3s4, $\Delta t$ under rk1 and rk2

[^rg-db3e7925d5ab]: $\boldsymbol\delta_i$ — the implicit solve's unknown in cell $i$ (total mass, normal momentum, [tangential momenta], energy)

[^rg-bd680c20cc4f]: $\vartheta$ — local phase $\pi h/\lambda_w$ of a wave of wavelength $\lambda_w$ in a Fourier error estimate; notation only; see @sec-appa

[^rg-e41403c7e700]: $\lambda_w$ — a wavelength (named); notation only; see @sec-appa

[^rg-d61c45b5aed8]: RK — Runge–Kutta

[^rg-c9f0740df1f4]: $\rho$ — total density, dry plus every species that carries mass [kg m$^{-3}$]

[^rg-41e20e055363]: $x_{1,i}$ — cell volume centroid ($r_{c,i}$ on spherical-polar)

[^rg-96220307ca24]: $r$ — $x_1$ on a spherical-polar grid (radius) [m]

[^rg-add6046816b3]: $\mathcal E$ — the conserved energy functional of a scheme, named each time ($\mathcal E = \sum_iV_iE_i+P$ under D, $\sum_iV_iE_i+\mathrm{PE}_d$ under the plain face form)

[^rg-0708b6d1b931]: $h_i$ — $x_1$ width of cell $i$, $x_{1,i+1/2}-x_{1,i-1/2}$; written $\Delta x_1$ where the direction must be explicit

[^rg-83a8e2b01f50]: $\Delta\mathbf U^{(0)}$ — the explicit stage increment handed to the implicit solve

[^rg-5fbd06ccd73e]: $\Delta\rho_i$ — the total density change solved by the implicit step, after redistribution and clamps; never the plain stage change, which is $\Delta^{\mathrm{stg}}\rho_i$

[^rg-bb05fe6a8840]: $A_{i\pm1/2}$ — $x_1$ face area

[^rg-20d0ad55a777]: YAML — YAML Ain't Markup Language, the structured input format used for decks

[^rg-9642e02413d9]: CI — continuous integration

[^rg-21882d810815]: CFL — Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
